t: Subtree Inversion Sum — Tree DP with Sign and Cooldown States
o: Inverting a node flips the sign of its whole subtree; two inversions on an ancestor–descendant chain must be at least k edges apart. Maximize the final total sum. Since effects nest along root-to-node paths, each node's value is multiplied by (+1 or -1) determined by how many of its ancestors were inverted. The distance constraint translates into a 'cooldown': after inverting a node, its descendants at depth less than k below cannot be inverted. With k ≤ 50, tracking cooldown 0..k per node is affordable. Examples confirm inversions in disjoint subtrees never conflict (Example 3 inverts siblings).
k: Each node's effective value is nums[u] times a sign inherited from inverted ancestors
Cooldown d = max(0, k − distance to nearest inverted ancestor); inversion allowed iff d = 0
Children are independent given the parent's (cooldown, sign) choice

a.i: dp[u][d][s] = maximum subtree-u sum when node u is entered with cooldown d (0 = free to invert) and inherited sign s (0 → +1, 1 → −1). If d > 0 we cannot invert here: value is ±nums[u] plus children with d−1. If d = 0 we take the better of not inverting (children keep d = 0, same sign) or inverting (value negated, children get cooldown k−1 and flipped sign). Children contribute independently because their internal choices don't interact across subtrees.
s: Build adjacency, root at 0, get a DFS order iteratively (n up to 5·10^4).
Process nodes in reverse DFS order computing dp[u][d][s] for d in 0..k, s in {0,1}.
For d>0: dp = sgn·nums[u] + Σ dp[child][d−1][s]. For d=0: max(no-invert branch, invert branch with sign flip and cooldown k−1).
a.t: O(n · k) time — each node fills 2(k+1) states, each merging its children in linear time overall since each child is visited once per parent state pair.
a.sp: O(n · k) for the DP table plus O(n) for the iterative DFS order.

w: The (cooldown, sign) DP is the intended solution; present it first in interviews. Key pitfalls: confusing 'distance ≥ k' with 'depth difference ≥ k' (it is the same thing on a tree path between ancestor and descendant), off-by-one on the cooldown after inversion (children start at k−1), and recursion depth — use an explicit stack in Python or risk TLE/stack overflow on path-like trees. Follow-ups: report which nodes to invert, handle k up to n, or generalize to DAGs where the constraint becomes LCA-based.
